original.title: Positive MEX imposes a literal journal ceiling and diagonal capacity bound
assumptions: Column h<N is live at START N.
K_N counts actual private diagonal awards; M_N is the maximum whole-row diagonal census before N.
Canonical positive MEX, nonreuse, FFD and whole-history blocker-host exclusion.

exactAuditedStatement: For h<N live at START N, let K count actual private diagonal awards on h<=t<N, including birth, S(t)=t+1-A(d(t)), M=max_{t<N}S(t), T_h=max_{a<h}d(a), u_i increasing diagonal labels, L=h+K+M and Z=max(T_h, u_(L+1)). Then max J_N(h)<=Z and K>=N-A(Z)-Imm(h).
hypotheses: N>=1 and 0<=h<N. The column is live at START N; in particular, no COPY occurs among its awards before N. Set T_0=0 for the empty seed set.
K includes future-owner diagonal awards; M is the whole-row diagonal census, not just ghosts.
proofDependencyMap: Shared canonical foundation: exact positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and P01-P12, independently reconstructed in ../CANONICAL-FOUNDATIONS.md with exact declaration mapping and game interpretation. DEPENDENCIES.json records the additional service lemmas. Final kernel receipts bind the source versions.
Whole-history blocker-host exclusion and FFD; exact journal cardinality.
independentDerivationAndChecks: The pre-N journal consists of h distinct seeds and N-h distinct private awards, disjoint by seed exclusion/nonreuse, total N labels. Its diagonal part has h+K labels.

For any private award z, literal positive MEX covers every diagonal label<z using its earlier journal and current left prefix. Their diagonal-label counts are at most h+K and M, so R(z-1)<=L. If z>u_(L+1) there would be L+1 such labels, contradiction. Seeds<=T_h supply the other ceiling.

Each eventually mortal a<h has a distinct blocker death sigma_a<d(a)<=T_h<=Z. Whole-history host exclusion forbids it from J_N(h), even when its death lies after N. Thus h-Imm(h) blockers inside[1, Z] are unavailable. Journal blocker count N-h-K<=A(Z)-(h-Imm(h)); rearrange.

No efficient recognition of future diagonal/blocker status is claimed. A dead/copied column would violate distinct-journal size and is excluded. Any slope-limit corollary requires the explicit existence premise; neither finite inequality supplies it.
